outcome: Pregnancy outcome (fetal/maternal complications, live births, recurrences)
cohort: 17 women previously treated for adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) who subsequently became pregnant (21 pregnancies) were compared with 247 non-pregnant ACC patients and a control group of 34 matched patients.
finding: Pregnancy in patients previously treated for ACC does not appear to be associated with a worse clinical outcome, with no severe fetal or maternal complications observed, except for one presumably unrelated cardiac malformation.
